name: Shudder to Think
label: Dischord
lede: A glam falsetto in a straight-edge town, an MTV Buzz Clip nobody saw coming, a run of film scores, and, twenty-seven years later, a new single back on Dischord.

eras.title: A hardcore band that shuddered to think
eras.text: Shudder to Think began as a teenage hardcore band and turned into something D.C. hadn't heard: punk played like theater, with a singer who went for falsetto instead of a bark. Dischord calls them part of a younger wave that grew up on the scene without copying it.

years.p: Bassist Stuart Hill and drummer [[Mike Russell|5052af59-8df4-485a-89ff-d34cd5314b0d]] form a hardcore band with guitarist Sam Fleming and singer Bobby Jones.

years.h: A new singer, spotted in a school play
years.p: Fleming and Jones leave for college. Hill brings in guitarist [[Chris Matthews|824d9e26-0d6b-4ec7-b7af-78505ed771b0]] from the new wave band 3-2-1, and Matthews suggests [[Craig Wedren|2da87294-e651-420b-8d25-2dbc3b29a285]], whom he'd seen perform in a school play.

years.h: The name comes from a car ride
years.p: Driving to practice, Russell says he shudders to think they'd end up just another hardcore band. The line becomes the name, and the music starts drifting toward post-hardcore.
The debut album, on the small Sammich label rather than Dischord.

eras.title: Glam in a straight-edge town
eras.text: On Dischord, Shudder to Think were the odd band out: melodic, theatrical and a little strange, on a label known for fury. By 1992 half the band had changed, and the new half came from Swiz and Jawbox.

years.p: Their first record for Dischord. The band had already turned up on the label's State of the Union compilation.
A second Dischord record, later paired with Ten Spot on one release (No. 55).
The guitarist leaves for school. [[Nathan Larson|c0845dd8-ef14-486c-92b6-260727732b4c]], who had played bass in [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], takes the guitar slot.
years.xp: Larson came over from [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], where he'd played bass, and switched to guitar. Within six months the drummer changed too, leaving Wedren and Hill as the only members from the 1980s records.

years.p: A show on the German tour becomes Your Choice Live Series Vol. 21, released by Tobby Holzinger's Your Choice label.

years.h: Russell's last show, and a drummer from Jawbox
years.p: Russell, there since the Stüge days, steps away. [[Adam Wade|d2502278-bf42-445b-98a2-9249af4c8a0a]], just out of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], takes over.
Their last album for Dischord before the move to a major.

eras.title: Buzz Bin, of all places
eras.text: Touring with Fugazi and The Smashing Pumpkins put them in front of far bigger crowds, and a major label came calling. They took it, becoming, by Dischord's count, one of only two bands ever to leave the label for a major.

years.h: On the road with Fugazi and the Pumpkins
years.p: Two very different tours in one year: the D.C. flagship and a Chicago band on its way to arenas.

q: We wanted our music to reach the most people and make a living.
years.p: Shudder to Think sign to Epic, championed by A&R man Michael Goldstone, and move to New York. [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] were the only other Dischord band to make the jump.
years.xp:
Wedren has said the reason was simple: they wanted to be heard by as many people as possible and to make a living at it. Looking back, the band has described the label as supportive throughout.

Not every fan agreed. Wedren told PopMatters that one picketed their show while they were opening for The Smashing Pumpkins, in defense of Dischord.

years.p: Produced by [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]] on analog tape in a big room for what the band called a widescreen sound. The drums were locked to a click they nicknamed the Russian Dragon. Angular, mathematical and nothing like its alt-rock shelf-mates. Per Wikipedia it had sold 30,000 copies in the U.S. by late October 1994, and 60,000 by February 1997.

years.cap: X-French Tee Shirt, the MTV Buzz Clip
q: I worshipped them. There was one year I saw them twelve times.
years.h: X-French Tee Shirt goes into heavy rotation
years.p: The video becomes an MTV Buzz Clip, the single reaches No. 36 on the Radio & Records alternative chart, and Rolling Stone takes notice. For a record this strange, it's a small miracle.
years.xp: PopMatters' look back dates the Buzz Bin run to spring 1995 and says Rolling Stone held it up as a sign the Buzz Bin had run its course. The song outlived the argument: [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]] would cover bits of it live, and [[Incubus|e3e0abcd-7671-4482-a9d8-462f5acc9be5]] played part of it at Lollapalooza 2003.

years.p: Shortly after promotion for Pony Express Record began, Wedren, then 26, was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma, he told Vanyaland in 2025. His doctor told him it was curable, and it was: Wikipedia says he fought it over the next few years and won.
years.xp: Wedren has said that at that age he didn't really grasp what the diagnosis meant. The band kept going, but the next album didn't land, and by 1998 the energy had moved to film scores.

years.p: In a 1995 interview, Buckley counts Shudder to Think among the bands he loves. [[James Iha|a89811cc-4514-48b2-b353-dba9debf7055]] of the Pumpkins calls them a wholly original rock band. So Into You comes out as an Epic single.

eras.title: From the stage to the screen
eras.text: The second Epic album missed, and the band's energy moved toward film. In one year they had songs across three movies, an invitation from Pearl Jam, and then no band.

years.p: The drummer from [[The Dambuilders|baf6c035-1e22-4a4c-ad4b-ea294fd41a1b]] replaces Adam Wade.
Mixed reviews and, in Wikipedia's words, a commercial flop. It's their second and last album for Epic.
Shudder to Think score High Art and First Love, Last Rites and land two songs in Todd Haynes' glam-rock film Velvet Goldmine. It's the road both Wedren and Larson will follow for decades.
years.xp:
High Art came out on Velvel and First Love, Last Rites on Epic's soundtrack arm. The Velvet Goldmine songs sat alongside the film's glam covers and originals.

After the band stopped, the film work became both men's day job: Wedren on David Wain's projects from The State circle, including Wet Hot American Summer and Reno 911!, and Larson on scores and his band Hot One.

years.p: Pearl Jam invite them on the Australian tour and slip a snippet of their song Pebbles into their own set.

years.h: Larson leaves, and that's the end
years.p: With Larson gone, Shudder to Think stop. Wedren goes on to score Wet Hot American Summer, School of Rock and later Yellowjackets; Larson scores films for Todd Solondz and Lilya 4-ever.

eras.title: Two coasts, two drummers
eras.text: The reunion was loose by design: a hired guitarist and bassist, and a different drummer depending on which side of the country they were playing. It ended with a farewell, then came back once more for a D.C. club's birthday.

years.p: Wedren, Larson and March play their first show in nearly a decade, with Mark Watrous on guitar and Jesse Krakow of Time of Orchids on bass.

years.h: March in the east, Wade in the west
years.p: The reunion keeps rolling. Kevin March drums the East Coast dates; Adam Wade comes back for the western ones, New Orleans included.
The reunion shows, documented.
A goodbye show in New York. Founding guitarist Chris Matthews joins them for the encore.
The Pony Express Record line-up of Wedren, Larson, Wade and Hill plays the D.C. club's anniversary, and Matthews and Russell join for the encore. Six members on one stage.

eras.title: Back on Dischord, twenty-seven years on
eras.text: Wedren survived a heart attack in 2018. Seven years later came something the reunions never offered: new songs. And the band that left Dischord for a major put them out on Dischord.

years.p: Wedren has described paramedics carrying him out on a stretcher at 2 a.m. while his son watched. He told Vanyaland it left him with years of night-time panic attacks, and a much stronger will to live.

years.h: Two surprise shows in Los Angeles
years.p: Wedren, Larson and Wade, with Clint Walsh on guitar and [[Jherek Bischoff|e0dcef88-0353-425c-99bd-81a36e96ed7f]] on bass, play Permanent Records Roadhouse and debut a new song, Playback.
Thirst Walk backed with Playback, the band's first new music since the late 1990s. Dischord takes preorders on the label site and Bandcamp.
Three new songs, digital, released the same night the band plays Philadelphia. New York follows on September 12 and Los Angeles on September 20, with the 7" repressed for the merch table.
